context: A police officer briefs a teen reporter about an investigation
purpose: Teach: 官房/省庁/起訴/告発/追及/朝刊/闘い/難民

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 今朝の朝刊を見たか？うちが捜査している事件が一面に出ている。
lines.en: Did you see this morning's paper? The case we're investigating is on the front page.
lines.style: Gruff officer voice, lowering tone with serious weight to set the mood.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、読みました。官房長官のお名前まで出ていて本当に驚きました。
lines.en: Yes, I read it. I was genuinely shocked the Chief Cabinet Secretary's name appeared.
lines.style: Eager teen reporter, polite and slightly nervous facing an authority figure.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 内部告発から動き出した捜査だ。関係省庁にも順次聴取を進めている。
lines.en: The investigation began from a whistleblower's tip. We're questioning relevant ministries one by one.
lines.style: Measured briefing cadence, professional pauses between key facts.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 起訴まで進む可能性は、現時点でどの程度あるのでしょうか？
lines.en: How likely is it, at this point, that the case will reach indictment?
lines.style: Curious cub reporter, pen poised, leaning forward respectfully.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 今は答えられん。容疑者の追及を続けている段階だからな。
lines.en: I can't answer that now. We're still in the stage of pressing the suspects.
lines.style: Stern, careful officer guarding case details with firm restraint.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 難民支援の予算が悪用されたという話も、本当なのですか？
lines.en: Is the rumor that refugee aid funding was misused also actually true?
lines.style: Voice rising with idealistic teen conviction and concern for justice.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 認否はできん。だが長い闘いになる。記者として覚悟しておけ。
lines.en: I can't confirm or deny. But this'll be a long fight. Brace yourself as a reporter.
lines.style: Stern mentor warning, fatherly gruff tone with weight on final words.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 肝に銘じます。本日はお時間を頂きありがとうございました。
lines.en: I'll take it to heart. Thank you very much for your time today.
lines.style: Formal respectful bow, slightly breathless closing from the young reporter.
